# Base-drift tolerant receipts (design, superseded)

Status: superseded, not implemented. The owner chose to bind a receipt to its diff instead of proving a base move harmless:
see [binding a receipt to its diff](local-review.md#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in) (protected `local_review.binding: "diff"`).
This document is kept as the record of the alternative that was considered.
`clouseau refresh` ([local review](local-review.md#refreshing-a-pull-request-after-its-base-moved)) already removes most of the
author's cost without touching trust; this document asks whether CI could also keep accepting a receipt after the base moved,
and recommends **go for a shadow stage and a narrow first stage, no-go for unconditional acceptance** (section 8).

## 1. Problem

A signed local receipt binds `snapshot.base_sha` and `snapshot.head_sha` (`verifySignedRecord`: `snapshot.base_sha === baseSha`).
When any other pull request merges, the base moves, every open pull request's receipt, assessment and approval is bound to
the old base, and `base-reconcile.cjs` posts `branch update needed`. The author's remedy is mechanical: merge the base,
review again, publish, edit the marker, push. A review costs several minutes and, in CI, about $6 (see
[receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md)); the human cost is the same for every open pull request after every merge.

The question: when the move of the base cannot have changed anything the review attested, can CI say so itself,
deterministically, without a model?

## 2. What a receipt binds to the base today

| Bound input | Where it enters | Drift behavior today |
|---|---|---|
| base commit id | `snapshot.base_sha`, `verifySignedRecord` | any move rejects |
| changed-file patches | `snapshot.files[].patch`, compared with GitHub's per-file `patch` (reviewed diff verification) | a patch that differs rejects |
| base-side sources | `snapshot.sources` with `ref: base_sha` (every changed file's base text, the contracts `readme` and `repository_policy`, `.clouseau-local.json`) | content is part of the signed snapshot |
| head-side sources | `snapshot.sources` with `ref: head_sha` | bound to the head |
| per-file history | `snapshot.history` (`git log -3` of the base for each changed path) | commit ids of the base |
| protected configuration | `config_digest` (`.github/clouseau.json` on the base) | read at the live base, so config drift already rejects |
| policy | `policy_digest`, engine revision and review semantics | independent of the base |
| lockfile summaries | derived from the base and head bytes, recomputed by CI | a lockfile moved on the base rejects |
| verification record | `technical` for the head | independent CI verification is separate and mandatory |
| owner confirmation | `/approve-intent` bound to the exact head | not carried by a receipt |

Almost every row is already content-addressed. What is really bound to the *commit id* of the base is a convenience, not
evidence; the evidence is the bytes the reviewers read.

## 3. The safe condition

`auto_approve` verdict means passing AI quality evidence eligible for signed
reuse, not technical approval. CI audit, workflow and container execution remains
independent; a local receipt does not claim those results or authorize GitHub
approval. CI must pass every mandatory technical gate before approval or merge.

A source-line reference can be normalized only to an existing immutable catalog
block containing that line. The controller preserves the observation and reads
the literal source bytes; this correction needs no additional model request.
Unknown sources, out-of-range lines and unsupplied blocks still stop review.

Reports and response journals stay outside source control. A completed identical
input is not automatically reviewed again. Fix blocking findings, commit the
changed implementation and reassess. A negative or incomplete review never
produces an approval receipt. This initial receipt path targets a new PR without
an unresolved existing GitHub review ledger; it rejects an existing incompatible
ledger rather than dropping its findings.

## Receipt-attested verification

A receipt signed by an enrolled identity attests the repository's whole declared verification. `clouseau review` runs every command of the
accepted base `.clouseau-local.json` (plus any `--additional-checks`) and, **before spending any AI review, refuses to sign** (non-zero exit,
no receipt, no marker) unless all of the following hold on the exact head:

- every command ran and exited 0 (a tool that is not installed, such as `cargo llvm-cov` or `coverage.py`, is a refusal that names the
  command and the missing tool, never a partial signature);
- native coverage was produced by this run;
- the coverage gate CI enforces passes: exact 100%, or for the protected `coverage.mode` of `changed_lines` the changed lines and branches are
  covered with no repository-wide regression (the base revision is measured locally in a temporary clean worktree, as CI measures it), or
  for `declared` the minimums declared at the base.

Declare every check you want skipped in CI (tests, coverage, fmt, lint, frontend, infrastructure) as a command of `.clouseau-local.json`.
Without an enrolled identity nothing is signed and the review remains advisory. The signed verification record then carries
`attestation: {version, recipe, commands, coverage_mode, gate: "passed"}`; receipts issued before this change carry none, stay valid for the
AI review, and attest no verification.

In CI, `operation: attested` (inputs `config`, `github-token`; output `attested`) answers `'true'` only when the pull request's receipt passes
every check the assessment applies (signature, enrolled key and author, expiry, exact head and base, engine, signed sources against live
GitHub; under the protected `binding: "diff"` the normalized diff and the live base's recipe instead of the head, base and sources, see
[binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)) AND attests the accepted base recipe. Anything else (no marker,
expired, wrong head without that binding, old receipt, an error) is `'false'`. Gate any

[renewed](#renewing-a-receipt-that-no-longer-verifies) (steps 3 to 5 below, no merge and no push of the branch). Under the
   protected `binding: "diff"`, when the pull request does not contain the base tip, a receipt that still covers its diff ends
   the command with `up_to_date` too, before anything is merged; otherwise the steps continue;
2. check with `git merge-tree` that the merge is clean, then **merge** the base (`git merge --no-ff`, message
   `Merge origin/<base> into <branch>`). There is no rebase and no force-push anywhere in the command;
3. run the ordinary local review of the head (`clouseau review`, including its verification) with the answers reused as
   described below, and sign the receipt. The claimed title of the change is the pull request's own title (GitHub's), not the
   subject of the merge commit, which is only `Merge origin/<base> into <branch>`; a pull request with no title is refused;
4. `clouseau publish` the receipt (this pushes only the artifact tag `clouseau-review/<nonce>`);
5. replace the `clouseau-local-review:v1` marker in the pull request body (appended when there is none);
6. `git push origin HEAD:<pull request branch>`, once, as the last step.

It refuses, with a message that names the cause and before pushing anything, when: the worktree has uncommitted or untracked
changes; HEAD is not the head GitHub reports for the pull request (when the local branch only has commits on top of that head, the message
says how many are unpushed and that you must `git push` first, then refresh again); the pull request is closed, comes from a fork, is not the
checked-out branch, or is not against the configured `base_branch`; the harness is unknown or its program is not installed;
the base conflicts with the branch (the checkout is left untouched and the conflicting paths are listed); a hook refuses the
merge (it is aborted). It never pushes when the review does not pass (`repair_required`, `review_incomplete`, ...), when a
passing review produced no signed receipt (no enrolled identity), when the checkout changed during the review, when the
pull request closed or got another head during the review, or when the push is rejected (the body is then restored). After
a review that does not pass, the merge commit stays in the local branch: repair, commit and refresh again, or run `git reset
--hard <old head>` to discard it. An agent-driven refresh that returns `awaiting_agent` is repeated with the identical
command; it recognises its own merge commit (the pull request head and a commit of the base as parents), does not merge or

that started the exchange ([pinning](#agent-driven-review-inside-an-ai-harness)): through the `clouseau` launcher the pinned engine
receives your own `refresh` command, resumes it and finishes it (review, publication, marker, push), and its result is what you
see. If the pinned engine fails, its error message is shown.

### Binding a receipt to its diff (opt-in)

By default a receipt is bound to the exact head and base commits it reviewed, so every merge to the base voids the receipt of
every other open pull request. With the protected `local_review.binding: "diff"` in `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch,
a receipt is bound to the **change** instead: it covers a pull request when the SHA-256 of the pull request's normalized diff
equals the SHA-256 of the normalized diff in the signed record (`src/receipt-patch.cjs`). The receipt format does not change:
the signed record already carries every patch.

The normalized diff is, per changed file in path order, its path, its status and (for a rename) its previous path, and its
hunks with every hunk header reduced to `@@`, so line numbers and git's trailing section text do not count. Every other byte
of a hunk counts, context lines and whitespace included. GitHub joins two git hunks that are one unchanged line apart; that
run of exactly seven context lines between two changes is split back into its two hunks on both sides. A summarized lockfile

contributes its path and status, and its derived summary is recomputed from the live lockfile bytes and must equal the signed
one apart from the revision it names.

| | Binding absent | `binding: "diff"` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a different head commit (GitHub's branch update, a merge of the base) | `receipt_revision_head` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| a different base commit | `receipt_revision_base` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| signed full-file sources compared with the live repository | compared | not compared: the signed record is what was reviewed; each source must still name a signed revision |
| lines added above a hunk on the base | `receipt_source` | covered |
| any change to an added, removed or context line, or to whitespace | `receipt_source` | `receipt_source`, naming the file |
| a file added, removed or re-statused, another rename | refused | refused, unchanged |
| a file without a GitHub patch | refused, unless the live sources prove it shows no text | refused, even an empty file or an identical rename: the live sources are not read |
| signature, enrolled key, author, expiry, repository, protected configuration and policy digests, engine and review semantics, passing decision | bound | bound, unchanged |

The test waiver follows the same binding: `operation: attested` answers `'true'` for a receipt whose diff matches and whose
signed `.clouseau-local.json` equals the live base's, so the tests are **not** rerun after a base move or an update-branch
merge. This is deliberate and has a cost: a break caused only by the base move (a semantic conflict between the reviewed change
and the new base) is found after merge, by the next run on the base. The run-consistency checks that compare the live pull
request between the assessment and the gate are unchanged; they protect one CI run from a push that lands mid-run.

`clouseau refresh` uses the same decision: under the binding it judges the receipt (including the diff, from the files GitHub
lists) before merging anything, and answers `up_to_date` whenever CI would accept it, rerunning nothing. A receipt that no longer
covers the diff is refreshed or renewed as usual. Where the binding applies: `verifySignedRecord` (the head and base comparison),
`verifySources` (revisions, sources, contract and verification refs, the lockfile summary, and the diff through `verifyPatches`),
and through them `screenReceipt`, `screenSources`, `receiptAttests`, `rehydrate` and `verifyRecord` (the record's revisions), and
`receipt-standing.cjs` and `pr-refresh.cjs`. An installation receipt is never diff-bound.

### Renewing a receipt that no longer verifies

When the base has not moved (or, under the diff binding, at any time), `refresh` does not answer `up_to_date` merely because nothing needs merging. It judges the
`clouseau-local-review:` marker in the pull request body for the unchanged head exactly as CI does: the same screening code
(`screenReceipt`, with the same signature, author, expiry, repository, head, base, protected configuration and policy, engine
and review-semantics checks) on the pull request as GitHub reports it now, the protected `.github/clouseau.json` of the fetched

in the marker or the receipt is trusted before it verifies. A repository whose protected configuration has no `local_review`
section has no receipts to judge and keeps the plain `up_to_date`.

by `binding: "diff"` never covers a file without a patch, because the live sources that would prove it empty are not read.

# Base-drift tolerant receipts (design, not implemented)

Status: design only. Nothing in this document is implemented, and nothing here changes what CI accepts today.
`clouseau refresh` ([local review](local-review.md#refreshing-a-pull-request-after-its-base-moved)) already removes most of the
author's cost without touching trust; this document asks whether CI could also keep accepting a receipt after the base moved,
and recommends **go for a shadow stage and a narrow first stage, no-go for unconditional acceptance** (section 8).

## 1. Problem

A signed local receipt binds `snapshot.base_sha` and `snapshot.head_sha` (`verifySignedRecord`: `snapshot.base_sha === baseSha`).
When any other pull request merges, the base moves, every open pull request's receipt, assessment and approval is bound to
the old base, and `base-reconcile.cjs` posts `branch update needed`. The author's remedy is mechanical: merge the base,
review again, publish, edit the marker, push. A review costs several minutes and, in CI, about $6 (see
[receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md)); the human cost is the same for every open pull request after every merge.

The question: when the move of the base cannot have changed anything the review attested, can CI say so itself,
deterministically, without a model?

## 2. What a receipt binds to the base today

| Bound input | Where it enters | Drift behavior today |
|---|---|---|
| base commit id | `snapshot.base_sha`, `verifySignedRecord` | any move rejects |
| changed-file patches | `snapshot.files[].patch`, compared with GitHub's per-file `patch` (reviewed diff verification) | a patch that differs rejects |
| base-side sources | `snapshot.sources` with `ref: base_sha` (every changed file's base text, the contracts `readme` and `repository_policy`, `.clouseau-local.json`) | content is part of the signed snapshot |
| head-side sources | `snapshot.sources` with `ref: head_sha` | bound to the head |
| per-file history | `snapshot.history` (`git log -3` of the base for each changed path) | commit ids of the base |
| protected configuration | `config_digest` (`.github/clouseau.json` on the base) | read at the live base, so config drift already rejects |
| policy | `policy_digest`, engine revision and review semantics | independent of the base |
| lockfile summaries | derived from the base and head bytes, recomputed by CI | a lockfile moved on the base rejects |
| verification record | `technical` for the head | independent CI verification is separate and mandatory |
| owner confirmation | `/approve-intent` bound to the exact head | not carried by a receipt |

Almost every row is already content-addressed. What is really bound to the *commit id* of the base is a convenience, not
evidence; the evidence is the bytes the reviewers read.

## 3. The safe condition

Let `B0`/`H0` be the signed base and head, `B1` the live base tip and `H1` the live pull request head. CI may accept the
receipt of `(B0, H0)` for `(B1, H1)` if and only if **all** of the following hold, each recomputed by CI from immutable

`auto_approve` verdict means passing AI quality evidence eligible for signed
reuse, not technical approval. CI audit, workflow and container execution remains
independent; a local receipt does not claim those results or authorize GitHub
approval. CI must pass every mandatory technical gate before approval or merge.

A source-line reference can be normalized only to an existing immutable catalog
block containing that line. The controller preserves the observation and reads
the literal source bytes; this correction needs no additional model request.
Unknown sources, out-of-range lines and unsupplied blocks still stop review.

Reports and response journals stay outside source control. A completed identical
input is not automatically reviewed again. Fix blocking findings, commit the
changed implementation and reassess. A negative or incomplete review never
produces an approval receipt. This initial receipt path targets a new PR without
an unresolved existing GitHub review ledger; it rejects an existing incompatible
ledger rather than dropping its findings.

## Receipt-attested verification

A receipt signed by an enrolled identity attests the repository's whole declared verification. `clouseau review` runs every command of the
accepted base `.clouseau-local.json` (plus any `--additional-checks`) and, **before spending any AI review, refuses to sign** (non-zero exit,
no receipt, no marker) unless all of the following hold on the exact head:

- every command ran and exited 0 (a tool that is not installed, such as `cargo llvm-cov` or `coverage.py`, is a refusal that names the
  command and the missing tool, never a partial signature);
- native coverage was produced by this run;
- the coverage gate CI enforces passes: exact 100%, or for the protected `coverage.mode` of `changed_lines` the changed lines and branches are
  covered with no repository-wide regression (the base revision is measured locally in a temporary clean worktree, as CI measures it), or
  for `declared` the minimums declared at the base.

Declare every check you want skipped in CI (tests, coverage, fmt, lint, frontend, infrastructure) as a command of `.clouseau-local.json`.
Without an enrolled identity nothing is signed and the review remains advisory. The signed verification record then carries
`attestation: {version, recipe, commands, coverage_mode, gate: "passed"}`; receipts issued before this change carry none, stay valid for the
AI review, and attest no verification.

In CI, `operation: attested` (inputs `config`, `github-token`; output `attested`) answers `'true'` only when the pull request's receipt passes
every check the assessment applies (signature, enrolled key and author, expiry, exact head and base, engine, signed sources against live
GitHub) AND attests the accepted base recipe. Anything else (no marker, expired, wrong head, old receipt, an error) is `'false'`. Gate any
workflow on it in a small job, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does:

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

### Binding a receipt to its diff (opt-in)

By default a receipt is bound to the exact head and base commits it reviewed, so every merge to the base voids the receipt of
every other open pull request. With the protected `local_review.binding: "diff"` in `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch,
a receipt is bound to the **change** instead: it covers a pull request when the SHA-256 of the pull request's normalized diff
equals the SHA-256 of the normalized diff in the signed record (`src/receipt-patch.cjs`). The receipt format does not change:
the signed record already carries every patch.

The normalized diff is, per changed file in path order, its path, its status and (for a rename) its previous path, and its
hunks with every hunk header reduced to `@@`, so line numbers and git's trailing section text do not count. Every other byte
of a hunk counts, context lines and whitespace included. GitHub joins two git hunks that are one unchanged line apart; that
run of exactly seven context lines between two changes is split back into its two hunks on both sides. A summarized lockfile

contributes its path and status, and its derived summary is recomputed from the live lockfile bytes and must equal the signed
one apart from the revision it names.

| --- | --- | --- |
| a different head commit (GitHub's branch update, a merge of the base) | `receipt_revision_head` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| a different base commit | `receipt_revision_base` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| signed full-file sources compared with the live repository | compared | not compared: the signed record is what was reviewed; each source must still name a signed revision |
| lines added above a hunk on the base | `receipt_source` | covered |
| any change to an added, removed or context line, or to whitespace | `receipt_source` | `receipt_source`, naming the file |
| a file added, removed or re-statused, another rename | refused | refused, unchanged |
| a file without a GitHub patch | refused, unless the live sources prove it shows no text | refused, even an empty file or an identical rename: the live sources are not read |
| signature, enrolled key, author, expiry, repository, protected configuration and policy digests, engine and review semantics, passing decision | bound | bound, unchanged |

# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
New to Clouseau? Start with the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md).
How a receipt stays valid across engine revisions: [receipt compatibility](docs/receipt-compatibility.md).
Every refusal or hold notice names its cause class and numbered next steps: [notices and their causes](docs/notices.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.
